pricing-rules.why: Strategy keeps each rule separate and lets new rules arrive without editing checkout. A switch works for two cases but grows into a change magnet; subclassing multiplies classes per combination.

order-events.why: Observer decouples the publisher from a growing list of subscribers. Direct calls work for one or two but couple Order to every team.

legacy-api.why: An adapter confines the translation to one place, so the rest of the code keeps its own interface.

add-behaviour.why: Decorators compose at runtime without a class per combination. Flags work for two options but tangle the class as options grow.

singleton-drawback.why: Passing the dependency in (injection) keeps the single instance without hiding it. Tests can then supply a fake.

state-pattern.why: For a few states, clear conditionals are fine. As states multiply, State objects keep each state's rules together. Judge by the problem's size, not the pattern's name.

open-closed.why: Extension points let new behaviour arrive as new code instead of edits to tested code.

composition.why: Inheritance couples a subclass to its parent's internals; composing small objects keeps parts replaceable.
